passages.text: INTRODUCTION We have elected to omit discussion on the earliest of the three years covered by the consolidated financial statements presented. Refer to Item 7. “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” and “Liquidity and Capital Resources” located in our Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended February 28, 2025, filed on April 23, 2025, for reference to discussion of the fiscal year ended February 29, 2024, the earliest of the three fiscal years presented. This MD&A, which should be read in conjunction with our Financial Statements, is organized as follows: Overview This section provides a general description of our business and brief descriptions of Fiscal 2025 goodwill and trademarks impairments, which we believe is important in understanding the results of our operations, financial condition, and potential future trends. Strategy This section provides a description of our strategy, including our 2025 Restructuring Initiative, and significant divestitures, acquisitions, and investments. Results of operations This section provides an analysis of our results of operations presented on a business segment basis. In addition, a brief description of significant transactions and other items that affect the comparability of the results is provided. Liquidity and capital resources This section provides an analysis of our cash flows, outstanding debt, liquidity position, and commitments. Included in the analysis of outstanding debt is a discussion of the financial capacity available to fund our on-going operations and future commitments, as well as a discussion of other financing arrangements. Critical accounting policies and estimates This section identifies accounting policies that are considered important to our results of operations and financial condition, require significant judgment, and involve significant management estimates. Our significant accounting policies, including those considered to be critical accounting policies, are summarized in Note 1. OVERVIEW Our internal management financial reporting consists of two business divisions: (i) Beer and (ii) Wine and Spirits and we report our operating results in three segments: (i) Beer, (ii) Wine and Spirits, and (iii) Corporate Operations and Other. In the Beer segment, our portfolio consists of high-end imported beer brands and ABAs. We have an exclusive perpetual brand license to produce our beer portfolio and to import, market, and sell such portfolio in the U.S. In the Wine and Spirits segment, we sell a portfolio comprised of exclusively higher-end wine and spirits brands. Amounts included in the Corporate Operations and Other segment consist of costs of corporate communications, corporate development, corporate finance, corporate strategy, executive management, human resources, internal audit, investor relations, IT, legal, and public affairs, as well as our investments such as those made through our corporate venture capital function . All costs included in the Corporate Operations and Other segment are general costs that are applicable to the consolidated group and are, therefore, not allocated to the other reportable segments. Certain Sands Family Stockholders have pledged shares of Class A Stock to secure various credit facilities. credit_strengths.text: The Beer segment's exclusive perpetual license for high-end imported and ABA brands underpins a premium portfolio with operating margin well above the Consumer Staples sector median, evidencing pricing power and brand equity that support stable cash generation through cycles.

Operating cash flow covers capital expenditure and dividends, with free cash flow after capex exceeding shareholder distributions, leaving a modest buffer for debt reduction or bolt-on investments without incremental borrowing.

key_risks.text: The Sands Family Stockholders retain significant influence via Class A stock and board nomination rights, and certain family holders have pledged shares to secure credit facilities; forced selling upon covenant noncompliance could pressure the equity price and complicate refinancing or strategic actions.

Debt maturities are concentrated in the next twelve months and year two, requiring refinancing or repayment; with cash modest relative to near-term maturities, the issuer depends on capital markets access or revolver capacity to manage the wall.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage remains comfortable and in line with the sector median, while net leverage sits above the sector median, indicating that debt service is manageable but the balance sheet carries more risk than peers.

Free cash flow to debt is below the sector median, and the indicative financial risk profile is Significant; a moderate EBITDA decline or debt increase would breach the next leverage threshold, leaving limited headroom for releveraging.

overall_credit_view.text: The issuer's premium beverage portfolio and strong operating margin support cash generation, but net leverage above the sector median and a Significant indicative financial risk profile temper the credit profile; we view the outlook as stable with limited cushion for adverse shocks.

Shareholder distributions absorb most free cash flow, constraining deleveraging; refinancing the near-term maturity wall is the key swing factor, and we would monitor capital markets access and any acceleration of buybacks or dividends.

credit_strengths.text: 啤酒分部的獨家永久授權涵蓋高端進口及ABA品牌，支撐優質產品組合，其營運利潤率遠高於消費必需品行業中位數，印證定價能力及品牌價值，支持週期性穩定現金產生。
營運現金流覆蓋資本開支及股息，扣除資本開支後自由現金流超過股東分派，留有適度緩衝用於減債或補強型投資而無需額外借貸。

key_risks.text: Sands家族股東透過A類股票及董事會提名權保留重大影響力，且部分家族持有人已質押股份以擔保信貸融資；若違反契約條款導致強制出售，可能對股價構成壓力，並使再融資或戰略行動複雜化。
債務到期集中於未來十二個月及第二年，需要再融資或償還；現金相對於近期到期債務規模有限，發行人依賴資本市場准入或循環信貸額度來管理到期牆。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率保持舒適並與行業中位數一致，而淨槓桿率高於行業中位數，表明債務償付可控但資產負債表風險高於同業。
自由現金流對債務比率低於行業中位數，指示性財務風險狀況為顯著；EBITDA適度下降或債務增加將突破下一槓桿率門檻，再槓桿空間有限。

overall_credit_view.text: 發行人的優質飲料產品組合及強勁營運利潤率支持現金產生，但淨槓桿率高於行業中位數及指示性財務風險狀況為顯著，削弱信用狀況；我們認為展望穩定，但應對不利衝擊的緩衝有限。
股東分派吸收大部分自由現金流，限制去槓桿；為近期到期牆再融資是關鍵搖擺因素，我們將監測資本市場准入及任何回購或股息的加速。
